version.changelog: Initial release: constraint-aware model recommendation with verified pricing and receipts

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed model-pricing and model-selection helper that uses an external API, with no hidden code, persistence, or destructive behavior in the artifact.

dimensions.detail: External API access is expected for a pricing index skill, and the artifact does not request local filesystem access, credentials, shell execution, broad indexing, or account mutation authority.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact declares an OpenClaw MCP server requirement for `inferenceindexer` and mentions a PyPI MCP server plus public config URL; no bundled executable installer or local setup script is present in the skill artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger wording is somewhat broad around model choice for 'any task,' but it remains tied to AI model/provider selection and cost checking rather than unrelated user activity.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No instructions create persistence, modify agent memory, install background services, escalate privilege, or alter future agent behavior beyond normal skill invocation guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to recommend and price-check AI inference models, and the instructions consistently focus on model ranking, provider endpoints, pricing, freshness, caveats, ZDR, and EU availability.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, understand that model-selection queries and constraints may be sent to the InferenceIndexer MCP/API, and applying returned endpoint configs may route inference through third-party providers. Review the MCP server/package separately if you need assurance about its runtime implementation or data handling.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger language was verified, but it is scoped to AI model/provider selection and cost optimization, so it is a quality/scope note rather than a security concern.
[E1] expected: The DeepInfra URL appears as an example provider endpoint returned by the model recommendation API; it is disclosed and aligned with the purpose of selecting inference providers.
[E1] expected: The InferenceIndexer URL is the disclosed API/key endpoint for the advertised service; this is expected network integration behavior, not hidden exfiltration in the artifact.
